# memcrumbs
> An open-source CLI that gives coding agents like Claude Code a project memory: a markdown wiki and a local index that answers in a few hundred tokens.

## About
memcrumbs is an open-source command-line tool, written in Python with only the standard library. It keeps a project's
working knowledge (standing rules, gotchas, runbooks, decisions, incidents and a dated journal) in short markdown pages,
and indexes those pages, your docs and your code symbols in a local SQLite FTS5 index. A coding agent reads a header of
rules once per session, then looks things up with `memcrumbs find` instead of reading whole files. It makes no model
calls and runs no background service; it uses the network only to update itself (`memcrumbs update`). License: Apache-2.0.

## What it does
- Session header: standing rules, project map, top gotchas and recent journal lines, capped at 1,000 tokens by default.
- `find`: ranked hits with path:line, age (`v12d`) and status (`STALE`, `SRC-CHANGED 3d`, `SUPERSEDED`, `REJECTED`).
- `page`, `outline`, `sym --body`: one section of a page, or one function by its line range.
- `about <file>`: the decisions, incidents and gotchas that cite a file.
- `fact <key>`: one current value per fact, optionally read from the source file.
- `decision`, `incident`, `log`, `rule`: structured records.
- `suggest`: offers (merges, missing pages, permission prompts for gotchas, skills), applied only on the user's yes,
  each undoable byte for byte. With transcripts on (`init` asks), task flows and pipelines the user repeats (the same
  steps in the same order in 3 tasks on 2 days, or in 6 tasks) become skill offers; the session header shows a count
  and the agent lists them when asked. Transcripts are read locally.
- `/memcrumbs-review` (a Claude Code skill): the owner approves agent-written rules, gotchas and pages in the session;
  Claude Code's permission prompt asks before each approval runs.
- Daily checks after slow commands: a secret-like value in the wiki is named (page only) in the session header.
- `check` and `scan`: wiki lint, and a secret scan of a folder, sdist or wheel.
- `init`: sets up the repository you are in with one command: names the project, drafts the map from the repo,
  indexes, wires Claude Code after one yes, runs `doctor`. Run again, it repairs; `init --remove` undoes it.
- `update`: upgrades memcrumbs, re-indexes and refreshes the wiring, and checks in a new process that it still starts.
- `wire`: connects a repository to Claude Code (CLAUDE.md block, session-start hook, skills, and ask rules so Claude
  Code asks the owner before each of their decisions, such as approving agent-written rules) or to agents that read
  AGENTS.md.

## Measured (repository benchmarks)
- A public repository before any wiki page is written (encode/httpx @ b5addb64): the answer in the top 3 for 75% of
  32 held-out questions written blind (code questions 90%), about 380 tokens per answer, against a median of 2,410
  for reading the one file that holds it. Method and data: https://github.com/mikedconcepcion/memcrumbs/tree/main/bench/httpx
- Recall@3 0.95 on 40 held-out questions written blind, on the invented sample project.
- About 450 tokens per lookup answer (mean over 100 sample questions, estimated as characters / 4).
- 10,000-file repository: full index 5-10 s, `find` 25-100 ms.
- CI: Linux, macOS and Windows with Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13.

## Install
pip install memcrumbs
cd <your repo> && memcrumbs init

## Upgrade
memcrumbs update
